text:
Maria: Heads up — telemetry shows ~0.4% of gold-tier requests are getting served from eu-west when us-west is congested. Compliance flagged a couple of customers.
Kevin: Can you paste an example request (headers + payload) so I can repro locally?
Maria: Yep, here's a sanitized sample:
```
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
  X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2
  X-Redwood-Tier: gold
  X-Redwood-Routing-Debug: on
Body: { "model": "gptx-3.1", "input": "..." }
```
Arjun: FYI the SDK sets X-Redwood-Region from the client config. Our fallback engine can override region for capacity/latency — what's the intended precedence right now?
Olivia: Design notes (old): explicit header > SDK param > account default > auto-fallback. We never implemented "respect_account_region_pin" consistently across all routing paths.
Kevin: :thinking_face: If a customer explicitly sets X-Redwood-Region it should be honored unless org policy forbids it. For gold customers we were planning forced fallback to meet SLOs though. That conflict might be the cause.
Maria: The odd part: console shows some accounts with region_pin=true but telemetry shows those still crossing region during model-variant fallback.
Arjun: Likely a bug: the model-variant fallback path calls the placement service directly and might skip account metadata checks. I'll add a middleware check.
deploy-bot: deploy: routing-service v2.14.0 canary -> prod-traffic 10% :rocket:
Olivia: We should also surface more routing telemetry. Proposal: when X-Redwood-Routing-Debug=on return response headers `X-Redwood-Chosen-Region` and `X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason`. That'll help support & customers.
Kevin: Also important: quota/cost attribution. If we route to eu-west but invoice/account expects us-west usage accounting, customers will dispute bills. We should attribute cost to pinned region when account.pin=true.
Maria: Legal prefers blocking cross-region by default for pinned accounts. We need a product decision: block vs allow-with-warning.
Arjun: Proposal: add account config `region_pin_strict` (boolean). If true -> block cross-region fallback and return 503 with code REGION_PIN_VIOLATION. If false -> allow fallback but tag telemetry and emit warning header `X-Redwood-Region-Warning`.
Olivia: UX: console toggle labeled "Enforce region pin (block cross-region fallback)" with an explanation and a default of off for self-serve. Enterprise defaults can be set via contract. We'll need a short explainer and changelog entry.
Kevin: SDK change: add optional param `region_enforcement=strict|warn|auto` mapped to header `X-Redwood-Region-Enforce`. SDK default should be `auto`. We'll document behavior and examples.
Maria: Action items: Arjun - PR for middleware check + tests; Kevin - SDK header mapping + changelog; Olivia - console toggle + help text; I'll draft customer comms for accounts that hit this. Let's sync tomorrow 10am.
deploy-bot: pr merged: #4523 routing-middleware-check
Olivia: I'll also add a support tool endpoint `/__debug/route-sim` so support can simulate fallback scenarios with given headers/params.
Maria: Thanks all — priority P1 for enterprise accounts. If anyone finds affected invoices escalate to finance and ops.
